candidate_sentences.text: The company reported a substantial decline in revenue and profitability during the 2025 reporting period compared to the prior year.
Consolidated revenue fell by 42.3 percent, dropping to EUR 310.9 million from EUR 539.0 million in 2024.

Despite the top-line contraction, gross profit margins remained relatively stable at 18.0 percent, while operating profit decreased to EUR 34.3 million, reflecting a normalization of margins following exceptional project completions in 2024.
Net profit attributable to equity holders stood at EUR 39.9 million, yielding a net margin of 12.8 percent.

verified_key_information_units.information: The 2025 revenue decline was driven by the completion of major projects initiated in prior years during 2025, combined with a slower pace of new contract signing in 2024 and the first half of 2025; this project cycle effect compressed profitability despite eventual improvement in contract signing activity later in 2025.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'In 2024, we were engaged in several large projects that had been started in earlier years, and these were completed as planned during 2025. The pace of signing new contracts was slower in 2024 and in the first half of 2025.'

candidate_sentences.text: This decrease was primarily driven by the completion of several large-scale construction contracts awarded in previous periods, which had elevated prior-year results.

verified_key_information_units.information: A major improvement in contract signing during the second half of 2025 resulted in the execution of Merko's largest-ever contracts for the Rūdninkai defence campus in Lithuania, which will contribute gradually to revenue starting in 2026 and provide stable workload for years ahead.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'the second half of 2025 showed a clear improvement, and preparatory efforts resulted in new major contracts... signing of the largest contracts in Merko’s history for the construction of two phases of the Rūdninkai defence campus... will begin to contribute to revenue gradually in 2026 and onwards.'

verified_key_information_units.information: The company expanded its public-private partnership (PPP) business through new real estate development agreements signed in 2025 for the Krulli quarter (Tallinn) and Uus-Karlowa quarter (Tartu), alongside continued success in the Noblessner area, enhancing long-term workload stability and diversification.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'Alongside the successful real estate development partnership in the Noblessner area of Tallinn, we signed two similar cooperation agreements in 2025 for the development of the Krulli quarter in Tallinn and the Uus-Karlowa quarter in Tartu. The Rūdninkai project marks a significant expansion of our PPP business Lithuania.'

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic investment in network companies operating under the Connecto brand delivered exceptional returns, accounting for one quarter (25%) of Merko's consolidated net profit in 2025 and substantially expanding operations in Latvia and Lithuania.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'A strategic decision made several years ago to invest in network companies operating under the Connecto brand has also clearly proven its value... in 2025 this investment in the joint venture accounted for as much as one quarter of Merko’s consolidated net profit.'

candidate_sentences.text: Additionally, investments in joint ventures operating under the Connecto brand contributed meaningfully to consolidated earnings.

verified_key_information_units.information: Residential construction activity surged due to improved consumer confidence across the Baltic region, with apartment construction starts exceeding three times the 2024 level, leading to 358 apartments sold (EUR 67.8 million) compared to 323 apartments (EUR 58.9 million) in 2024 and inventory buildup to 1,169 units.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'in 2025 we were able to start construction of more than three times as many new apartments as in 2024.' Operating result section: 'A total of 358 apartments (incl. 11 apartments in a joint venture) were sold in 2025 at the total value of EUR 67.8 million... compared to 323 apartments... and EUR 58.9 million in 2024.' Consolidated Statement of Financial Position: Inventory section shows apartment inventory of 1,169 units as at 31.12.2025.

candidate_sentences.text: Conversely, the real estate development segment showed resilience, with revenue rising to EUR 73.4 million and apartment deliveries increasing to 358 units.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K5, K6, K7, and K8 are all adequately represented in the candidate summary with core material meaning covered. K3 and K4 are missing entirely - there is no mention of Merko's largest-ever contracts for the Rūdninkai defence campus or new real estate development agreements in Krulli and Uus-Karlowa quarters. While the summary covers most high-priority financial and operational themes, the absence of these two major strategic developments means the overall picture is incomplete, justifying a 'Generally yes' score rather than 'Yes'.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected: the decline in revenue is explained by completed contracts (S1-S3), financial metrics are consistently presented (S2, S4-S6, S15-S16), segment performance is contrasted (S7-S8), market conditions are analyzed (S11-S13), and forward-looking indicators are provided (S9-S10, S18). There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, organizational issues, or unnecessary repetition. The summary forms a clear narrative from performance decline to strategic positioning.
